translationRepairs: After Han pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing wanted to continue Wu with the son of Marquis De, and continue Chu with Prince Yuan's son Liu Li.
After Han pacified Wu and Chu, Emperor Jing wanted to continue Wu with the son of Marquis De, and continue Chu with King Yuan's son Liu Li.
Although this unit abbreviates the name to 禮, the genealogy identifies King Yuan's son as Liu Li (劉禮); retaining the surname supports correct identity resolution.
King Zhao Liu Sui—his father was Gaozu's middle son, named You, posthumously titled "You."
King Zhao Liu Sui—his father was Gaozu's middle son, whose personal name was You and whose posthumous title was You, "the Secluded."
The personal name You and posthumous title You represent different Chinese words; naming each category and translating the latter distinguishes them without inserting Chinese into the English field.
Empress Dowager Gao installed Lu Lu as King of Zhao, but within a year she passed away.
Empress Dowager Gao installed Lü Lu as King of Zhao, but within a year she passed away.
呂祿 is the Lü surname; idiomatic Lu Lu loses the umlaut and conflates it with unrelated Lu surnames, while Lü Lu matches the Chinese and the unit's own literal.
